title: The cross-sectional stock return predictions via quantum neural network and tensor network
abstract_summary: This preprint evaluates quantum circuit learning (a quantum neural network) and tensor network (a quantum-inspired model) for cross-sectional monthly stock return prediction, comparing them to linear regression and classical neural networks. Using TOPIX500 constituents and portfolio backtests over about a decade, the authors find the tensor network outperforms classical benchmarks, while the quantum circuit learning model shows competitive excess returns in recent market conditions though lower risk-adjusted performance overall, suggesting these methods can capture nonlinear feature interactions.
methodology_description: The study evaluates quantum and quantum-inspired machine learning methods for cross-sectional monthly one-month-ahead stock return prediction on the TOPIX500 universe (Japanese equity market). Inputs are n=10 firm-level features (value, quality, momentum, size, market measures) cross-sectionally ranked each month (rank/(Nt-1)) and, where required, normalized to the encoding range for quantum circuits. Models compared are: ordinary linear regression (OLS), two feed-forward neural networks (NN1: layers (10,7,1), NN2: (10,5,4,1) with ReLU), a variational quantum circuit learning model (QCL) implemented as a parameterized quantum circuit simulated noiselessly, and a tensor network model using a matrix product state (MPS) with bond dimension m=2. All models are trained to minimize mean squared error (MSE) on training data using gradient-based optimization (Adam optimizer; parameter-shift rule for QCL gradients); the tensor network is trained via gradient descent rather than DMRG. Backtesting is done monthly from June 2008 to May 2021 using a rolling scheme: models are trained on the most-recent 3-year window and then used to predict returns for the subsequent 1-year period; models are re-estimated once per year. At each month, stocks are ranked by predicted return, and an equal-weight long portfolio of the top quintile is formed; portfolio performance is compared to the TOPIX500 benchmark via annualized excess return (ER), tracking error (TE), and information ratio (IR). Implementations use Qulacs for quantum circuit simulation, TensorFlow for neural networks and optimization, and TensorNetwork for the MPS implementation. Numbers of model parameters were kept comparable across non-linear models to enable fair comparison.
algorithms_used: Variational Quantum Circuit Learning (Quantum Neural Network, VQA)
experimental_setup: Noisy quantum hardware was not used; QCL was implemented and executed on a noiseless quantum circuit simulator (Qulacs). Neural networks and tensor network implementations used TensorFlow and TensorNetwork libraries. All training used gradient-based optimizers (Adam) with 20 epochs; QCL gradients computed via the parameter-shift rule.
dataset_used: Monthly data for constituents of the TOPIX500 index (Japanese equities) from June 2008 to May 2021. Universe is the TOPIX500 constituents (≈500 most liquid Japanese stocks). Ten input features per stock: Book-value-to-price, Earning-to-price, Sales-to-price, Return-on-equity, Momentum (1m, 3m, 6m, 12m), log(Market Capitalization), and 60-month Beta. One-month forward returns are predicted. Data are not publicly released by authors due to licensing.

experiment_input.source: TOPIX500 constituents (Tokyo Stock Exchange), proprietary data (license-restricted)
experiment_input.universe_size: Up to 500 stocks (TOPIX500 constituents; universe varies over time)
experiment_input.preprocessing: Cross-sectional ranking of each feature at each time step: feature value -> rank / (Nt - 1). Inputs for quantum circuit encoding normalized to the required range ([-1,1]). Returns computed as one-month forward simple returns.

pipeline_steps: At each annual re-estimation point: gather the most recent 3 years of monthly training data (features and realized one-month returns).
Preprocess features by cross-sectional ranking (rank/(Nt-1)); normalize for QCL encoding range.

Train models (Linear: OLS; NN1/NN2: feed-forward networks with ReLU; QCL: parameterized quantum circuit; TN: MPS) to minimize MSE between predicted and realized returns. Use Adam optimizer for NN, QCL and TN; 20 training epochs for ML models. For QCL use parameter-shift rule to compute gradients. For TN gradient-descent is used (DMRG noted but not used).
Hold out subsequent 1-year period as test/prediction period (monthly predictions).
Each month in the test period: compute predicted returns for all stocks; rank stocks by predicted return; form equal-weight long portfolio of top quintile stocks; compute realized portfolio return.
Compute monthly excess return over TOPIX500 benchmark and aggregate performance metrics (ER, TE, IR) over the backtest period.

quantum_model_specification.encoding_circuit: Per-qubit rotations V(x) = Prod_j RZ_j(arccos(x_j^2)) RY_j(arcsin(x_j)) with inputs normalized to [-1,1].
quantum_model_specification.ansatz: Repeated layers U(θ) = (for i=1..d) [per-qubit RX(θ_{i,j,1}) RZ(θ_{i,j,2}) RX(θ_{i,j,3}) on each qubit] with an interleaved fixed Urand = exp(-i H τ) entangling layer; depth d=3.
quantum_model_specification.measurement: Expectation value of Pauli Z on first qubit used as model output.

training_protocol.rolling_scheme: Train on 3-year window, test on following 1-year window; re-estimate once per year across entire June 2008–May 2021 period.
training_protocol.optimizer: Adam (all ML models); gradient descent for TN; parameter-shift for QCL gradients

portfolio_formation.positioning: Long equal-weight top quintile (20%) of predicted-return ranking

Tabulated ER, TE, IR per model
experiment_output.format: Tabular performance metrics and cumulative return time-series plots comparing each model's portfolio to TOPIX500

experiment_parameters.measurement: Expectation of Pauli Z on first qubit (QCL)

results_summary: The study reports empirical backtests (TOPIX500, June 2008–May 2021) comparing linear regression, two small neural networks, a tensor-network (TN) model, and a simulated quantum circuit learning (QCL) model. The TN model achieved the best overall performance (ER 3.71%, TE 5.41%, IR 0.69) despite having the fewest parameters. QCL produced positive excess return but with higher volatility and lower information ratio than the best classical neural network over the full period; in the 2016+ subperiod QCL and TN both improved materially and outperformed the classical neural nets. Experiments were run on simulators with 10 features and modest model sizes, and the authors frame interpretations about non-linearity capture and overfitting control as hypotheses requiring further investigation.
performance_claims: Full period (June 2008–May 2021) results (Table 2): Linear ER -0.28% TE 6.64% IR -0.04; NN1 ER 1.27% TE 3.79% IR 0.34; NN2 ER 1.76% TE 4.28% IR 0.41; QCL ER 1.35% TE 6.18% IR 0.22; TN ER 3.71% TE 5.41% IR 0.69.
Post-2016 subperiod results (Table A1): Linear ER -0.12% TE 7.82% IR -0.02; NN1 ER 0.56% TE 3.48% IR 0.16; NN2 ER 0.18% TE 4.31% IR 0.04; QCL ER 2.63% TE 5.85% IR 0.45; TN ER 4.20% TE 5.14% IR 0.82.

Model sizes and settings: QCL used 10 qubits, circuit depth d=3, 90 parameters; TN used bond dimension m=2, 76 parameters; NN models had ~92–93 parameters. Training used Adam optimizer for 20 epochs and mean-squared-error objective.
quantum_advantage_detail: The paper reports that a simulated quantum circuit learning model (QCL) and a quantum-inspired tensor network (TN) showed competitive or superior performance in specific backtests, but QCL was only run on a noiseless simulator (no hardware) and TN is a classical, quantum-inspired method. The observed gains are dataset- and configuration-specific, limited to 10 features and modest parameter counts, and do not constitute a demonstrated, general quantum computational advantage; the authors frame potential advantages (non-linearity capture, overfitting control) as hypotheses needing further empirical validation.

key_ideas: #idea:quantum-advantage — A variational quantum circuit learning (QCL) model produces competitive excess returns in recent market conditions, though its risk-adjusted performance (information ratio) is lower than some classical baselines.

#idea:quantum-advantage — A tensor-network (MPS) model, a quantum-inspired classical approach, outperforms classical neural networks and OLS on cross-sectional monthly return prediction and portfolio backtests.

#idea:hybrid-approach — The QCL is trained in a hybrid fashion: parameterized quantum circuit simulated via Qulacs with gradients obtained by the parameter-shift rule and classical Adam optimizer for parameter updates.

#idea:near-term-feasibility — Experiments use small-depth ansatz (depth d=3) and per-qubit encoding for 10 features, implemented on a noiseless simulator, indicating potential near-term exploratory studies but without real-hardware validation.
#idea:hybrid-approach — Comparable parameter counts across nonlinear models were enforced to enable fair comparison between QCL, classical NNs, and MPS.
#idea:near-term-feasibility — Practical deployment faces data-encoding and scaling considerations (cross-sectional ranking, normalization to [-1,1], per-qubit rotations encoding).
contradictions: contradiction:classical-vs-quantum — The quantum circuit learning model did not clearly outperform classical neural networks on risk-adjusted measures, and a quantum-inspired tensor-network (classical MPS) outperformed both classical NNs and QCL, contradicting a straightforward claim that quantum methods (as implemented) provide superior predictive or portfolio performance.

contradiction:classical-vs-quantum — Findings suggest quantum-inspired classical models (MPS) can match or exceed performance of simulated QCL in this financial task, challenging narratives that quantum models automatically yield advantage for cross-sectional return prediction.
